maze-puzzles.title: Hard Maze Puzzles for Kids – Printable PDF
maze-puzzles.metaDescription: Hard maze puzzles for kids: narrow roads, long routes and deep dead ends in picture scenes. 24 challenging mazes for grades 1-2, printable as PDF.
maze-puzzles.p1: When the easy mazes stop being a challenge, these are the next step. Every maze here is drawn as a picture scene, with roads winding through a garden, a jungle, a harbor or a town, and a clear goal at the end: help the seahorse find the seaweed, bring the rocket to the planet, find the shortest way to the haystack. The hard level keeps the same idea as the easier mazes but makes the path work harder for the child.
maze-puzzles.p2: At the hard level the roads are narrower, the way to the goal is longer, and there are more dead ends, and deeper ones, that look tempting until the very last turn. Some pages add a rule on top of the maze: collect every ear of corn on the way, hop across stepping stones in ABC order, step only on sums that make 10, or follow tangled kite strings to find whose kite is whose. Because a rule never changes from level to level, a child who has done the easy version of a page already knows the task and can focus on the harder route.
maze-puzzles.p3: These mazes suit first and second graders who enjoy a puzzle and have the patience to plan ahead. Encourage children to trace the route with a finger first and only then use a pencil. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child draws the way with a finger or mouse. Hard mazes make a good early-finisher task, a quiet brain break, or a challenge for children who race through the easier pages.

dot-dot-hard.title: Hard Dot-to-Dot Worksheets – Skip Counting Pictures
dot-dot-hard.metaDescription: Hard dot-to-dot worksheets: count by 2s, 5s and 10s, count back from 20, small numerals and complex outlines. 24 printable pages for grades 1-2.
dot-dot-hard.p1: A dot-to-dot becomes a real math task when the numbers do not simply go 1, 2, 3. On many of these harder pages, children join the dots by counting by twos, by fives, by tens, or backwards from 20, and a picture appears only if every step of the count is right. Skip a number and the outline breaks, so the picture itself tells the child whether the counting was correct.
dot-dot-hard.p2: The hard level changes how much help the page gives. The numerals are smaller, there is no number strip at the top to look things up, and the outlines are more detailed, with more dots and tighter corners. On the open counting pages the whole count is in play: up to 40 when counting by twos, up to 100 by fives and up to 200 by tens. The pictures come from our illustrated scenes, with the hero of each scene drawn in dots and the rest of the picture stepping aside so every number sits on clear paper.
dot-dot-hard.p3: These pages fit first and second grade, when skip counting is practiced and children need many repetitions without it feeling like a drill. Children who find the hard level tricky can start with the easy level of the same page, which has big numerals, a number strip and simple outlines. A finished picture is easy to check at a glance, which makes these pages handy for independent work, morning work or early finishers.

find-the-differences-easy.title: Easy Spot the Difference Pictures for Kids (PDF)
find-the-differences-easy.metaDescription: Easy spot the difference pictures for kids: two scenes side by side with big, clear changes. 24 pages for preschool to grade 2, printable as PDF.
find-the-differences-easy.p1: Two pictures that look the same, but a few things have changed: spot the difference is a picture puzzle children recognize at once. On these easy pages each scene is an original illustration, from a farm and a snowy hill to a jungle, a kitchen and the sea floor, and the changes are big and easy to see once you look carefully. Children compare the two pictures, find what is different and mark it.
find-the-differences-easy.p2: The easy level is set by how busy the scene is and how big the changes are. The scenes have fewer things in them, and each difference is large enough for a young child to spot without straining. The collection includes several kinds of pages: classic find-seven-differences scenes, pages that ask how many differences there are, pages where children tick the words that name what changed, and mirror pictures to fold and check. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child taps each difference.
find-the-differences-easy.p3: Spot the difference trains careful looking, visual memory and attention to detail, skills that later help with reading and spelling, where a small change in a letter changes the word. The easy pages suit preschool to first grade; the ten-difference and writing pages suit first and second graders. When a child finds every difference quickly, the same scenes are available at harder levels with busier pictures and smaller changes. They work well as a calm table activity, a center, or a quiet moment at the end of the day.

color-by-number-easy.title: Easy Color by Number Worksheets for Kids (PDF)
color-by-number-easy.metaDescription: Easy color by number worksheets: big areas and 3 to 5 colors, with animals, the sea, the savanna and the desert. 24 pages for preschool and kindergarten.
color-by-number-easy.p1: Color by number turns coloring into a small reading-and-matching task. Every area of the picture has a number, and the color key shows which color goes with which number. On these easy pages the pictures are cheerful scenes, a rabbit in the forest, a whale in the sea, a duck on the pond, a camel in the desert, and the finished picture appears area by area as the child follows the key.
color-by-number-easy.p2: The easy level is set by how complex the picture is. The areas are big and there are only three to five colors, so young children can keep track of the key without getting lost and can stay inside the lines. Each page is a different illustration, and the collection mixes scenes in the sea, the garden, the savanna and the desert with single big pictures such as a fox, a cupcake and a teddy bear. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child taps an area to fill it with color, which works well on a tablet or an interactive whiteboard.
color-by-number-easy.p3: Easy color by number pages suit preschool and kindergarten, when children are learning to recognize numbers and colors. Point to each number in the key together and say it aloud before coloring starts. When a child manages these confidently, the same kind of pictures are available at harder levels with more colors and smaller areas. The pages make a calm table activity, a center, or a gentle start to the morning.

logic-grid-puzzles.h1: Hard Logic Grid Puzzles for Kids
logic-grid-puzzles.title: Hard Logic Grid Puzzles for Kids – Printable
logic-grid-puzzles.metaDescription: Hard logic grid puzzles for kids: only not clues, either-or clues and crossed-out pictures. 24 challenging picture logic puzzles for grades 2-3.
logic-grid-puzzles.p1: In a logic grid puzzle, children read a few clues about who has what and use a grid to work out the answer step by step. These picture puzzles use farm animals, fruits, pets and other familiar themes: each child in the puzzle has one picture, and the clues decide which. The fun is in the reasoning: one clue rules something out, the next clue narrows it down, and suddenly the whole grid falls into place.
logic-grid-puzzles.p2: The hard level makes every clue work harder. There are no simple yes clues that fix a whole row at once. Instead the clues say what someone does not have, sometimes turned around (the cat does not belong to Mia), or offer an either-or with no yes clue at all. The grid shows crossed-out pictures only, and the true-or-false pages include statements such as "nobody has …" and "either … or …". The collection includes picture clue puzzles, three-clue puzzles, 4 by 4 grids with six clues, two-attribute puzzles and read-the-grid pages.
logic-grid-puzzles.p3: These puzzles suit second and third graders who have done a few easier logic puzzles and are ready for a stretch. Teach children to mark every no with a cross as soon as a clue rules it out; the answer usually appears from what is left. Many puzzles also have an on-screen version where the child ticks and crosses the grid. They make a strong early-finisher challenge and a good partner task.

maze-puzzles-easy.title: Easy Maze Puzzles for Kids – Printable PDF
maze-puzzles-easy.metaDescription: Easy maze puzzles for kids: wide roads, short routes and few dead ends in picture scenes. 24 mazes for preschool, kindergarten and grade 1, as PDF.
maze-puzzles-easy.p1: A first maze should feel like a small adventure, not a frustration. Every maze here is a picture scene with a clear goal: help the monkey find the banana, help the mouse reach the cheese, help the hamster get to the apple, find the shortest way to the doctor. The roads wind through the picture, and the child follows them with a finger or a pencil until the character reaches the goal.
maze-puzzles-easy.p2: The easy level makes the maze friendly for young children. The roads are wide, the way to the goal is short, and there are only a few dead ends, none of them deep. Some pages add a simple rule: pick up every acorn on the way, hop across stepping stones in ABC order, or follow kite strings to find whose kite is whose. Because the rule stays the same at every level, a child who masters the easy version can move straight to the harder version of the same page.
maze-puzzles-easy.p3: Mazes train planning, visual tracking and pencil control all at once, which makes them a good pre-writing activity in preschool and kindergarten. In first grade the easy pages work as a warm-up before the harder levels. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child draws the way with a finger or mouse. Encourage children to look ahead before drawing and to go back calmly when they reach a dead end.

sight-words-in-sentence.title: Sight Words in Sentences Worksheets (PDF)
sight-words-in-sentence.metaDescription: Sight words in sentences: fill the sight word into sentences, build one sentence step by step and trace the sentences. 24 easy pages for K-1.
sight-words-in-sentence.p1: Knowing a sight word on a flash card is one thing; reading it inside a sentence is what children actually need. These worksheets put each sight word to work in real sentences. Children read short sentences, trace the missing sight word into each gap, and trace whole sentences, so the word becomes something they read in context, not just a word on a list.
sight-words-in-sentence.p2: There are three kinds of pages. Sight Word in Sentences asks the child to fill the word into several short sentences. One Sentence Step by Step takes a single sentence and has the child read it, complete it, trace it, circle the sight word and finally write it. Trace the Sentences gives a set of sentences to trace with the sight word in each one. These are all easy-level pages, with fewer and shorter sentences and the word traced in the gap. Every sight word on the list has its own pages, so you can match the worksheet to the word your class is learning this week.
sight-words-in-sentence.p3: The pages suit kindergarten and first grade, alongside the sight word list you already use. Introduce the word first, read the sentences aloud together, then let children work on their own. When the easy level is comfortable, the same pages exist at a harder level with longer sentences, capital-letter gaps and look-alike words to tell apart.

tracing-pictures-easy.title: Easy Tracing Pictures for Kids – Printable PDF
tracing-pictures-easy.metaDescription: Easy picture tracing worksheets: dashed pictures to trace with short, simple lines. 24 pages for preschool and kindergarten, printable as PDF.
tracing-pictures-easy.p1: Picture tracing is often the very first pencil work a young child does, and it should feel like making a picture, not doing an exercise. On these pages, every picture is drawn in dashed lines that lie right on top of the real drawing: a bakery, a rainy crossing, a hen and her chick, a fish in its tank. The child follows the dashes with a pencil, and the picture appears line by line.
tracing-pictures-easy.p2: The easy level is lighter: there is clearly less to trace than on the standard page, so a young child can finish a picture before the hand gets tired. The collection mixes many kinds of pages: first tracing pictures with big, round shapes, look-then-trace pages, scenes to complete, picture words, where-do-I-start pages that show the start points, pages that practice down, across and slanted lines, the other half of a picture, and simple big, middle and small comparisons.
tracing-pictures-easy.p3: Easy tracing pages suit preschool and kindergarten. They build pencil control, the habit of starting at the right point, and the steady, controlled movements children need later for letters and numbers. Let children color the picture once the tracing is done; that keeps the motivation high. When the easy pages go smoothly, the same kinds of pictures are available at a harder level with more to trace.

tracing-pictures-hard.title: Hard Tracing Pictures for Kids – Printable PDF
tracing-pictures-hard.metaDescription: Harder picture tracing worksheets: busy scenes with more lines to trace, for kindergarten and grade 1. 24 dashed-line pictures, printable as PDF.
tracing-pictures-hard.p1: Once a child can trace a simple picture with confidence, busier scenes are the natural next step. On these harder pages the dashed lines still lie right on top of the real drawing, but the pictures are fuller: a busy harbor, a repair garage, a castle meadow, the deep sea, a flower garden. The child follows every dashed line with a pencil until the whole scene is complete.
tracing-pictures-hard.p2: The hard level is heavier: there is clearly more to trace than on the standard page, with more lines, more small details and longer stretches of steady pencil work. The collection includes full scenes, picture words, hidden-animal scenes where tracing reveals who is hiding, what-is-inside pages, and the other half of a picture to complete. Because the pictures are detailed, these pages also train patience and the ability to keep going on one task for longer.
tracing-pictures-hard.p3: Hard tracing pictures suit kindergarten children who breeze through the easier pages and first graders who need more fine-motor practice. Remind children to start each line where the dashes begin and to keep the pencil moving smoothly rather than in short scratches. A finished page can be colored afterward, which turns the work into a picture they are proud to take home.

multiplication-tables-hard.title: Hard Times Tables Worksheets – Missing Factors
multiplication-tables-hard.metaDescription: Harder multiplication table worksheets: find the missing factor or product and mixed facts. 24 pages for grades 2-3, printable as PDF.
multiplication-tables-hard.p1: When children know their times tables in order, the next step is using them flexibly. These harder worksheets mix the facts up and hide different parts of each equation, so children cannot simply count along a sequence. They have to know the fact, or work it out from one they know.
multiplication-tables-hard.p2: At the hard level, the missing number can be a factor or the product: 6 × ? = 42 as well as 6 × 7 = ?. The facts are mixed rather than in order, which shows quickly which ones are secure and which still need work. The collection covers the tables from 2 to 10, with separate pages for single tables, including the harder tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9, and general times tables practice. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
multiplication-tables-hard.p3: These pages suit second and third graders who have practiced the tables in order and are ready to recall the facts in any order. A good routine is a short daily page rather than one long session. When a fact keeps causing trouble, go back to the easy level of that table, where the facts are in order and a few are already worked, and build up again.

multiplication-tables-easy.title: Easy Times Tables Worksheets – 2, 5 and 10
multiplication-tables-easy.metaDescription: Easy multiplication table worksheets: the tables of 2, 5 and 10 and single tables in order with worked examples. 23 pages for grades 2-3, as PDF.
multiplication-tables-easy.p1: The first times tables a child learns should feel easy, and the tables of 2, 5 and 10 are the natural place to start because they follow patterns children already know from skip counting. These worksheets begin there and give the support children need while the tables are still new.
multiplication-tables-easy.p2: At the easy level there are two kinds of pages. Some mix only the easy tables, 2, 5 and 10. Others take a single table and go through it in order, with the facts for ×1, ×5 and ×10 already worked, so children can use them as anchors to find the rest. The collection includes the single tables from 2 to 10 as well as general times tables practice. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
multiplication-tables-easy.p3: These pages suit second graders meeting multiplication for the first time and third graders who need to firm up the basics. Encourage children to say each fact aloud and to use the worked facts as stepping stones: if 5 × 4 is 20, then 6 × 4 is one more 4. When a table goes smoothly at this level, the same table is available at the standard and hard levels, where the order changes and the missing number moves.

division-with-remainders-easy.title: Easy Division with Remainders Worksheets (PDF)
division-with-remainders-easy.metaDescription: Easy division with remainders: picture pages, practice rows, find the error and number-line pages, all with small divisors. 24 pages for grade 3.
division-with-remainders-easy.p1: Division with remainders makes sense the moment children see it: put things into equal groups, and whatever cannot make a full group is left over. The picture pages let children see and count every remainder. Children ring the groups, count how many groups there are and how many are left over, and write the division.
division-with-remainders-easy.p2: At the easy level the divisors are small, dividing by 2 or by 3, and the piles of pictures are small too, so children can focus on the idea of a remainder rather than on big numbers. There are two kinds of picture pages: Ring the Groups, where children circle equal groups in a pile, and Share It Out, where they deal the pictures out fairly and see what is left. The pictures come from many themes, from fruit and animals to the beach and the bakery. Number pages complete the set: practice rows, exact or not, find the error, and hopping back on a number line, all with small divisors and fewer rows. Many pages also have an on-screen version.
division-with-remainders-easy.p3: These pages suit third graders meeting remainders for the first time, and children who find the abstract version hard to follow. Start with real objects, counters or blocks, then move to the pictures, then to number-only problems. When the easy level is secure, the standard and hard levels use bigger divisors, more scattered piles and sharing among more people.

how-draw-easy.h1: Easy How to Draw Worksheets for Kids
how-draw-easy.title: Easy How to Draw Worksheets for Kids (PDF)
how-draw-easy.metaDescription: Easy how to draw worksheets: step-by-step drawings with a grid, copy each step, order the steps and draw in a picture. 24 pages for K-2, as PDF.
how-draw-easy.p1: Drawing step by step shows children that a picture is built from simple shapes, one line at a time. These worksheets break each drawing into a few steps, from a camper and a rocket to a dog, an owl and a seahorse. New lines in each step are shown clearly, so children can see exactly what to add next.
how-draw-easy.p2: The collection includes several kinds of drawing lessons. With the grid pages, children copy a drawing square by square. In the picture pages they draw the animal or object into a scene. Order the steps asks them to put the steps in the right order before drawing. Copy each step lets them draw along with each stage. Other pages ask children to finish a drawing, draw from simple shapes, or draw and then write the word. All of the pages here are at the easy level of their lesson.
how-draw-easy.p3: Easy how-to-draw pages suit kindergarten through second grade. They build careful looking, spatial thinking and pencil control, and many children who say they cannot draw are surprised by what they produce when the steps are clear. Let children color the finished drawing or add a background of their own. The drawings also make a gentle writing prompt: draw the animal, then write one sentence about it.

dot-dot-easy.title: Easy Dot-to-Dot Worksheets for Kids – Printable
dot-dot-easy.metaDescription: Easy dot-to-dot worksheets: big numerals, a number strip and simple outlines, counting by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s. 24 printable pages for K-1.
dot-dot-easy.p1: Joining the dots in the right order is counting practice that ends in a picture. On these easy pages, children follow the numbers from dot to dot, and a character from one of our illustrated scenes appears: an animal, a vehicle, a little hero standing on the ground. If a number is skipped, the outline breaks, so the picture shows whether the count was right.
dot-dot-easy.p2: The easy level gives plenty of support. The numerals are big and clear, a number strip at the top shows the sequence so children can check which number comes next, and the outlines are simple, with the character standing on its own. The collection includes one-to-twenty pages and skip-counting pages, counting by twos, fives and tens, as well as counting back from 20, all at the friendliest level.
dot-dot-easy.p3: These pages suit kindergarten and first grade, when children are learning the counting sequence and starting to skip count. Let children say each number aloud as they draw, and color the picture once it is finished. When the easy pages are comfortable, the same pages exist at a harder level with smaller numerals, no number strip and more detailed outlines. Counting aloud while drawing also helps children hear where the number sequence goes wrong.

compound-words.title: Hard Compound Words Worksheets – Grade 2 (PDF)
compound-words.metaDescription: Harder compound words worksheets: split compounds into two words and play compound detective with text-only words. 10 pages for grades 1-2.
compound-words.p1: Sunflower, raincoat, toothbrush: compound words are two words joined into one, and spotting the two parts helps children read and spell longer words. These harder worksheets give children compounds without picture support, so they have to recognize the two words inside each one by reading.
compound-words.p2: There are two kinds of pages. Split the Compound asks children to find the two words that make each compound and write them separately. Compound Detective has children hunt for compound words, link the parts that belong together and build new compounds. At the hard level, there are more words to link and the words are text only, drawn from longer word lists rather than the simplest everyday compounds. Many pages also have an on-screen version.
compound-words.p3: These pages suit second graders and confident first graders who have done the easier compound word pages with pictures. Encourage children to cover one half of the word with a finger and read each part on its own. A useful extension is to ask children to invent their own compound words and draw what they would mean. Children love hearing that a butterfly is not really made of butter, and that conversation is the best way into the idea. Silly compounds stick in the memory.

word-problems-hard.title: Hard Word Problems for Kids – Grades 1 to 3 (PDF)
word-problems-hard.metaDescription: Harder word problems: missing starts, compare problems, bigger numbers and mixed multiplication and division. 24 pages for grades 1-3, as PDF.
word-problems-hard.p1: A word problem is hard when the story does not simply tell you what to do. These harder pages are written so that children have to think about the story before they calculate. Each one is a short story about something familiar, from accessories and baking to Christmas, and children read it, decide what is being asked and write the answer.
word-problems-hard.p2: There are two groups of pages. In the addition and subtraction problems, the hard level moves the unknown: sometimes the change is missing (7 + ? = 12, with only the start pictured), and sometimes two amounts are compared, asking how many more or how many fewer. In the multiplication and division problems, the numbers are bigger, up to 30 or 36, the sharing and grouping pages carry three stories, and the mixed page has no pictures at all, because a picture would give away whether to multiply or divide. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
word-problems-hard.p3: These pages suit first graders who are confident with simple stories, and second and third graders who need a real challenge. Teach children to retell the story in their own words before they write a number sentence. A labeled answer sentence at the end shows whether the story was really understood.

logic-grid-puzzles-easy.h1: Easy Logic Grid Puzzles for Kids
logic-grid-puzzles-easy.title: Easy Logic Grid Puzzles for Kids – Printable
logic-grid-puzzles-easy.metaDescription: Easy logic grid puzzles for kids: yes clues, two clues per puzzle and picture grids. 24 picture logic puzzles for grades 1-2, printable as PDF.
logic-grid-puzzles-easy.p1: Logic grid puzzles teach children to reason step by step: read a clue, rule something in or out, and use what is left. These easy puzzles are a gentle first step. Each puzzle has a few children and a few pictures, from farm animals and fruits to pets, and the clues tell you which child has which picture.
logic-grid-puzzles-easy.p2: The easy level is built for beginners. The clues are yes clues that fix a whole row and column at once (Mia has the cat), each puzzle has only two clues, the grid uses ringed pictures to show the answer, and the true-or-false pages have just four statements to judge. The collection includes picture clue puzzles, two-clue puzzles, puzzles with yes, no and either-or clues, two-attribute puzzles and read-the-grid pages. Many puzzles also have an on-screen version where the child ticks and crosses the grid.
logic-grid-puzzles-easy.p3: These puzzles suit first and second graders meeting logic grids for the first time. Solve one together on the board, thinking aloud: if Mia has the cat, then nobody else does. After a few puzzles, most children can work on their own. When the easy level feels simple, move on to the standard level, and then to the hard level, where the clues only say what someone does not have.

read-and-color-easter.title: Read and Color Easter Worksheets – Grade 1 (PDF)
read-and-color-easter.metaDescription: Read and color Easter worksheets: read the sentence, count the pictures and color them. 8 black-and-white pages in three levels for grades 1-2.
read-and-color-easter.p1: Read and color turns an Easter coloring page into a reading task. Next to the pictures of eggs, bunnies, chicks and baskets, short sentences say how many things to color and in which color. The child reads the sentence, counts out the right pictures and colors them. The finished page shows at a glance whether every sentence was read carefully.
read-and-color-easter.p2: The collection has eight black-and-white pages in three levels, and the levels change the reading load. At the easy level there are fewer pictures and smaller numbers. At the hard level the numbers are bigger, and pictures of other things are mixed in among the ones to color, so the child has to read and count precisely. There is also a busy-page version with one big picture and a list of sentences to follow.
read-and-color-easter.p3: These pages suit first graders who can read short sentences on their own, and second graders who need careful reading practice. They make a calm Easter task for centers, morning work or the last days before spring break. For children still building confidence, read the sentences together first and then let them count and color on their own. Because a child who reads too quickly colors the wrong number, these pages are a good, gentle check of careful reading.

spot-the-difference-zoo.h1: Spot the Difference at the Zoo
spot-the-difference-zoo.title: Spot the Difference Zoo Pictures for Kids (PDF)
spot-the-difference-zoo.metaDescription: Spot the difference at the zoo: find seven differences between two zoo scenes, at the standard and hard levels. Three printable pages for K-2.
spot-the-difference-zoo.p1: A day at the zoo, drawn twice, with a few small changes: on these pages children compare two zoo scenes side by side and find the seven differences. Something has disappeared, something has changed color, something has moved. The child looks carefully, compares the two pictures part by part and marks every change.
spot-the-difference-zoo.p2: There are three pages, all original zoo illustrations. One is at the standard level and two are at the hard level, where the scene is busier and the changes are smaller, so children have to search more systematically. The levels are set by how much is going on in the picture and how big each change is. Each page also has an on-screen version where the child taps the differences, which works well on a tablet or an interactive whiteboard.
spot-the-difference-zoo.p3: Spot the difference builds careful looking, attention to detail and visual memory. The zoo pages suit kindergarten through second grade and fit naturally into an animal unit or the days before a class trip to the zoo. Teach children to scan the picture in a fixed order, left to right and top to bottom, so no part is missed. When a child finds all seven differences, ask them to describe each one in a sentence.

opposites-hard.title: Hard Opposites Worksheets – Antonyms for Grade 1-2
opposites-hard.metaDescription: Harder opposites worksheets: no word bank, more picture pairs, sentences and prefix antonyms with un-, dis- and in-. 17 pages for grades 1-2.
opposites-hard.p1: Big and small, open and closed, happy and sad: opposites are one of the first ways children learn to compare and describe. These harder worksheets take away most of the help, so children have to come up with the opposite themselves rather than pick it from a list.
opposites-hard.p2: At the hard level each kind of page asks more. Write the Opposite Word has no word bank. Opposites with Pictures has eight picture pairs instead of four. Opposites in a Sentence has eight sentences with no bank. Pair Up the Opposites includes two words that have no partner, so children must check every pair. Opposite or the Same? offers four words to choose from instead of two. The prefix page, antonyms with un-, dis- and in-, has ten rows without the prefix list. Many pages also have an on-screen version.
opposites-hard.p3: These pages suit confident first graders and second graders who have done the easier opposites pages. Talk about why two words are opposites, and notice that some words have more than one opposite depending on the sentence. The prefix page is a good bridge to spelling: once children see that unhappy is the opposite of happy, they can build many more words the same way.

pre-writing-worksheets-circles.title: Pre-Writing Worksheets Circles and Shapes (PDF)
pre-writing-worksheets-circles.metaDescription: Pre-writing worksheets for circles, squares, triangles and diamonds, in three levels and many themes. 15 printable pages for preschool and K.
pre-writing-worksheets-circles.p1: Circles are one of the hardest shapes for small hands: the pencil has to keep turning smoothly and end where it began. These pre-writing worksheets practice circles together with squares, triangles and diamonds, the shapes children need before they can form letters like o, a, d and g. In each row the child traces the shape again and again, following dashed shapes or a model depending on the level.
pre-writing-worksheets-circles.p2: The fifteen pages come in three levels, and the levels fade the help. At the easy level every shape in the row is dashed and has its own start dot. At the standard level a model is followed by dashed shapes. At the hard level there is a model, one dashed shape, and then only start dots, so the child draws the rest independently. The pages use many themes, from body parts and sports to tools, birds, pets and the sea, and about half are black and white so children can color the pictures afterward.
pre-writing-worksheets-circles.p3: These pages suit preschool and kindergarten. Practice each shape big in the air or with a finger on the table before the pencil comes out, and watch where the child starts each circle: starting at the top and going counterclockwise is the habit that later makes letters easier. When a child traces the easy page smoothly, move to the same theme one level up.

spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.h1: Spot the Difference Under the Sea
spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.title: Spot the Difference Under the Sea for Kids (PDF)
spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.metaDescription: Spot the difference under the sea: compare two ocean scenes and find the differences. Three easy printable pages for preschool to grade 1, as PDF.
spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.p1: Fish, coral, seaweed and a little submarine: these spot the difference pages take children under the sea. Each page shows the same ocean scene twice, and a few things have changed between the two pictures. Children compare the scenes carefully and mark every difference they find.
spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.p2: There are three pages, all at the easy level, where the scenes are not too crowded and the changes are big enough for young children to find. Two pages ask children to find seven differences in an underwater scene, and one page, with a submarine, has three differences, which makes it a good first page for the youngest children. The level is set by how busy the scene is and how big each change is. Each page also has an on-screen version where the child taps the differences.
spot-the-difference-under-the-sea.p3: These pages suit preschool, kindergarten and first grade and fit well into an ocean or summer unit. Spot the difference builds careful looking and visual memory. Encourage children to name each difference aloud: the fish has changed color, the shell is missing. That turns the puzzle into vocabulary practice too. Children who enjoy these can move on to busier sea scenes at the harder levels. Enjoy the dive.

telling-time-worksheets-easy.title: Easy Telling Time Worksheets – Clocks with Extra Help
telling-time-worksheets-easy.metaDescription: Easy telling time worksheets: fewer clocks and options, the minute hand printed and minute numbers around the clock. 24 pages for grades 1-3, as PDF.
telling-time-worksheets-easy.p1: Reading an analog clock is a big step for young children: two hands, two different meanings, and numbers that stand for hours and minutes at the same time. These easy worksheets give children the support they need while the clock is still new, starting with whole hours and half past.
telling-time-worksheets-easy.p2: At the easy level each page gives extra support: fewer clocks, fewer answer options, the minute hand already printed where children draw the hands, and the minute numbers written around the clock face so children can see that the 6 means 30 minutes. The collection starts with whole hours and half past (On the Hour, Half Past What?, Clock Partners, Draw the Clock Hands) and also has easy versions of the quarter-hour, five-minute, to-the-minute, elapsed-time and 12- and 24-hour pages. Many pages also have an on-screen version where children tap the time, type the hour or drag the hands.
telling-time-worksheets-easy.p3: The hour and half-hour pages suit first graders learning to tell time; the minute, elapsed-time and 24-hour pages suit second and third graders who need extra support. A real clock with movable hands is the best companion: set a time, let the child read it, then check it on the page. When whole hours and half past are secure, the standard and hard levels add more clocks, plain clock faces, quarter to and the tricky misreadings to watch out for.

color-by-number-hard.title: Hard Color by Number Worksheets for Kids (PDF)
color-by-number-hard.metaDescription: Hard color by number worksheets: 6 to 8 colors and many small areas, with vehicles, farm animals and town scenes. 24 pages for grades 1-2.
color-by-number-hard.p1: Color by number becomes a real test of patience when the picture has many small areas and a longer color key. On these harder pages, every area still has a number, and the key still says which color goes with which number, but there is much more to keep track of. The pictures include a rocket at night, an ice cream truck, a race car, a fire truck, farm animals, town scenes and a sea turtle.
color-by-number-hard.p2: The hard level is set by how complex each picture is: six to eight colors and many parts, some of them small, so children have to check the key carefully and color precisely. Each page is a different illustration. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child taps an area to fill it with color, which suits tablets and interactive whiteboards. Because the picture only looks right when every number is followed, the finished page shows how carefully the child worked.
color-by-number-hard.p3: These pages suit first and second graders who enjoy coloring and have mastered the easier pages. They are a good calm activity for early finishers, indoor recess or the end of the day. Suggest that children color one number at a time across the whole picture rather than area by area: it is faster and leads to fewer mistakes. Sharp colored pencils help with the smallest areas.

rhyming-words-easy.title: Easy Rhyming Words Worksheets for K-1 (PDF)
rhyming-words-easy.metaDescription: Easy rhyming words worksheets: rhyme and write, sort the rhymes, finish the rhyme and rhyme strings with fewer choices. 24 pages for K-1, as PDF.
rhyming-words-easy.p1: Hearing that cat and hat rhyme is an early sign that a child is starting to listen to the sounds inside words, a skill that matters a great deal for learning to read. These easy rhyming worksheets give children lots of practice in hearing and matching rhymes, with pictures to support every word.
rhyming-words-easy.p2: At the easy level each kind of page is made simpler. Rhyme and Write has fewer choices. Sort the Rhymes has fewer bins to sort into. Finish the Rhyme puts word choices under each verse. Rhyme Strings uses a word bank with nothing to reject. Write Your Own Rhymes asks for one rhyme each. Many pages also have an on-screen version, except Write Your Own Rhymes, which stays on paper because every child's answer is different.
rhyming-words-easy.p3: These pages suit kindergarten and first grade. Before children work on their own, say the words aloud together and listen for the part that sounds the same at the end. Clapping or tapping the rhyming part helps many children hear it. When the easy pages are comfortable, the standard and hard levels add near-miss words such as cat and cap, which sound almost alike but do not rhyme. Rhymes in songs help too.

rhyming-words-hard.title: Hard Rhyming Words Worksheets – Near Misses
rhyming-words-hard.metaDescription: Harder rhyming words worksheets: near-miss foils like cat and cap, pictures that fit no bin and three rhymes each. 24 pages for grades 1-2.
rhyming-words-hard.p1: Once children can hear an obvious rhyme, the real test is telling a true rhyme from a word that only sounds close. These harder rhyming worksheets are built around exactly that: words that almost rhyme, pictures that belong nowhere, and fewer cues to lean on.
rhyming-words-hard.p2: At the hard level each kind of page asks more. Rhyme and Write includes a near-miss foil, such as cap offered for cat. Sort the Rhymes adds near-miss pairs and pictures that fit no bin at all. Finish the Rhyme gives no picture cue and only one word box. Rhyme Strings asks for three rhymes for each word, and Write Your Own Rhymes shows the word alone. Many pages also have an on-screen version, except Write Your Own Rhymes, which stays on paper.
rhyming-words-hard.p3: These pages suit confident first graders and second graders who need to sharpen their listening. When a child chooses a near miss, say both words slowly and listen to the last sound together: cat ends with t, cap ends with p. That careful listening is exactly what helps later with spelling. The hard pages also make a good small-group activity, where children can argue their case for each word. If a choice is close, say both words aloud again.

number-of-the-day-easy.h1: Easy Number of the Day Worksheets
number-of-the-day-easy.title: Easy Number of the Day Worksheets (PDF)
number-of-the-day-easy.metaDescription: Easy number of the day worksheets: smaller numbers, one more and one less, ten frames and teen numbers. 20 printable pages for kindergarten and grade 1.
number-of-the-day-easy.p1: Number of the day is a short daily routine with a big effect: one number, looked at from many sides. On each page children write the number, show it with drawings, find the numbers that come just before and after, and build it in different ways. Done every day, it builds a deep sense of how numbers work.
number-of-the-day-easy.p2: At the easy level the numbers are smaller, and the page asks for one more and one less rather than bigger jumps. For teen numbers, the ten is already shown in a full ten frame, so children only add the ones. Where the page asks for ten more and ten less, ten frames sit beside the questions to help. The collection includes the classic number of the day, pages for teen numbers, pages for ten more and ten less, and pages for numbers up to 99, all at the easy level, with every answer kept within 99.
number-of-the-day-easy.p3: These pages suit kindergarten and first grade, as a morning routine or a math warm-up. Use the class calendar or the school day count to choose the number, and fill in one page together before children try one alone. When the easy pages go smoothly, the standard and hard levels use bigger numbers, counting back in tens and number lines with fewer printed numbers.

sight-words-easy.title: Easy Sight Words Worksheets for K-1 (PDF)
sight-words-easy.metaDescription: Easy sight words worksheets: read, trace and write, sight word of the day, sentences and find the word, with short sentences. 24 pages for K-1.
sight-words-easy.p1: Sight words are the small, frequent words children need to recognize instantly to read fluently: the, and, said, was. These easy worksheets give each word plenty of friendly practice, from reading and tracing it to finding it in sentences, so it becomes automatic.
sight-words-easy.p2: The collection mixes several kinds of pages, all at the easy level. Read, Trace, Write works through a set of words at once. Sight Word of the Day focuses on one word: read it, trace it, write it and use it in sentences. Sight Word in Sentences and One Sentence Step by Step put the word to work in context. Trace the Sentences and Find the Sight Word, where children color and count the word in a group, round out the set. At the easy level the sentences are fewer and shorter, and the word is traced in the gap rather than written from memory. The word list grows to about 100 high-frequency words.
sight-words-easy.p3: These pages suit kindergarten and first grade, alongside the sight word list your class already uses. Introduce a word, read it together in a sentence, then let children practice on the page. A few minutes a day works better than a long session once a week. When the easy level is comfortable, the hard level has longer sentences, capital-letter gaps and look-alike words.

word-problems-easy.title: Easy Word Problems for Kids – Grades 1 to 3 (PDF)
word-problems-easy.metaDescription: Easy word problems for kids: small numbers, picture support, addition and subtraction within 10 and first multiplication stories. 24 pages, as PDF.
word-problems-easy.p1: A good first word problem is a short story a child can picture. These easy worksheets tell small stories about familiar things, from a trip to the bakery to Christmas presents, and ask children to work out the answer. Pictures support many of the stories, so children can see what is happening before they write a number sentence.
word-problems-easy.p2: There are two groups of pages. In the addition and subtraction problems, the easy level keeps the numbers within 10, and on the within-10 pages the second number is 2 or 3, so children can count on. In the multiplication and division problems, the easy level uses small numbers, up to 12 to 20, with big pictures that show the groups. The collection includes picture word problems, addition and subtraction stories, problems within 10, and first multiplication, grouping and sharing stories. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
word-problems-easy.p3: The addition and subtraction pages suit first graders; the multiplication and division pages suit second and third graders meeting those operations. Read the story aloud together first, then ask what is happening and what we need to find out. Drawing a quick sketch is a good habit at this stage. When the easy level is secure, the standard and hard levels move the unknown and add comparison problems.

mental-math-hard.title: Hard Mental Math Worksheets – Grade 1 and 2
mental-math-hard.metaDescription: Harder mental math worksheets: crossing ten, the unknown first and three-number problems within 20. 24 pages for grades 1-2, printable as PDF.
mental-math-hard.p1: Mental math is about knowing number facts so well that you can use them without counting on your fingers. These harder worksheets push beyond the easy facts to the ones that need real strategies: crossing ten, working backward from the answer, and keeping three numbers in mind at once.
mental-math-hard.p2: On the pages to 20, the problems cross ten, as in 8 + 5 or 13 − 6, which pushes children to use strategies like making ten. The unknown often comes first, as in ? + 4 = 11, and some problems use three numbers. The collection includes mental math to 10 and to 20, missing-number problems to 20, and addition and subtraction practice to 20. Every page is designed so the equations fill their cards, with clear spacing that keeps the focus on the numbers. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
mental-math-hard.p3: These pages suit first graders who know the facts within 10 well and second graders building fluency within 20. Talk about strategies rather than just answers: to solve 8 + 5, take 2 from the 5 to make 10, then add 3. A short page every day builds fluency faster than a long session once a week, and the same page can be repeated a few days later to see the progress.

verb-forms.title: Hard Verb Forms Worksheets – Past Tense Grade 2
verb-forms.metaDescription: Harder verb forms worksheets: verb tables without hints, irregular verbs, choosing the right form and verbs in sentences. 24 pages for grade 2.
verb-forms.p1: Walk becomes walked, but go becomes went: verb forms are where grammar starts to get interesting, and where the irregular verbs trip children up. These harder worksheets give children less support and more to do, so they have to know the forms, not just copy a pattern.
verb-forms.p2: At the hard level each kind of page asks more. The verb tables come two at a time, with no given form and no hint. Match the Verb to Its Past Form has seven verbs. Verb Forms in Sentences with Pictures has eight sentences. The Irregular Verbs page, with be, have, do and go, gives no forms and asks for four sentences. Choose the Right Verb Form has nine rows with three forms each, and Find the Verb has nine sentences. Many pages also have an on-screen version.
verb-forms.p3: These pages suit second graders who have done the easier verb pages and are learning the past tense in earnest. Read the sentences aloud: the wrong form often sounds wrong even before a child can explain why. Keep a small chart of the irregular verbs on the wall while children work, and take it away once the forms are secure. Short, regular practice works best for these.

synonyms.title: Hard Synonyms Worksheets – Grade 2 (PDF)
synonyms.metaDescription: Harder synonyms worksheets: synonyms for said, shades of meaning, synonym pairs and word cards with harder words. 24 pages for grade 2, as PDF.
synonyms.p1: Synonyms give children choices: instead of saying big again, they can say huge, large or enormous, and their writing comes alive. These harder worksheets ask children to choose between words carefully, notice small differences in meaning and pick the word that fits best.
synonyms.p2: At the hard level each kind of page asks more. The synonym word cards use eight harder words. Synonyms with Pictures shows four pictures with five tags to place. Synonym Pairs has eight pairs with more verbs. Shades of Meaning has six rows without the strength key, so children decide on their own whether a word is a little or a lot. Synonyms for Said has six sentences and two extra words that fit none of them. Many pages also have an on-screen version.
synonyms.p3: These pages suit second graders who have done the easier synonym pages. Ask children to say each sentence with each word and decide which sounds best, and talk about why whispered and shouted are both ways of saying something but are not interchangeable. The said page connects directly to writing: after the worksheet, ask children to use three new words for said in their next story. Collect the words on a class chart so children can use them again.

alphabetical-order-hard.title: Hard ABC Order Worksheets – Same First Letter
alphabetical-order-hard.metaDescription: Harder alphabetical order worksheets: number the words, then write them, and sort words that start with the same letter. 20 pages for grades 1-2.
alphabetical-order-hard.p1: Putting words in ABC order is easy when every word starts with a different letter. It becomes a real skill when two words start the same way and you have to look at the second letter. These harder worksheets give children that challenge across many themes, from the beach and camping to emotions, tools and the farm.
alphabetical-order-hard.p2: There are three kinds of pages. Number the Words asks children to number a list of words from first to last in alphabetical order. Number Them, Then Write Them adds a second step: after numbering, children write the words out in order. When Words Start the Same groups words with the same first letter, so children have to compare the second letter, and sometimes the third, to sort them. Some pages are in color and some are in black and white.
alphabetical-order-hard.p3: These pages suit first and second graders who know the alphabet well and can sort words by their first letter. Keep an alphabet strip in view while children work, and teach them to underline the first letter that is different between two words. Sorting by the second letter is exactly the skill children will need later to use a dictionary or a glossary.

read-and-color-christmas.title: Read and Color Christmas Worksheets – Grade 1
read-and-color-christmas.metaDescription: Read and color Christmas worksheets: read the sentences, count and color the pictures. Nine black-and-white pages in three levels for grades 1-2.
read-and-color-christmas.p1: Read and color turns a Christmas coloring page into a reading task. Next to the pictures of bells, candles, stockings and gifts, short sentences say how many things to color and in which color. The child reads each sentence, counts out the right pictures and colors them. If a sentence is read too quickly, the wrong number gets colored, so the finished page shows how carefully the child read.
read-and-color-christmas.p2: The collection has nine black-and-white pages in three levels, and the levels change the reading load. At the easy level there are fewer pictures and smaller numbers. At the hard level the numbers are bigger, and pictures of other things are mixed in among the ones to color. There are also variations: a page where the sentences are all mixed up and must be found, a page with four sentences, and a busy page with one big picture and a list of sentences to follow.
read-and-color-christmas.p3: These pages suit first graders who can read short sentences on their own and second graders who need careful reading practice. They make a calm task for December centers, morning work or the last days before winter break. For children still building confidence, read the sentences together first and then let them count and color on their own. The colored page also makes a cheerful decoration for the classroom.

find-the-differences-kitchen.h1: Find the Differences in the Kitchen
find-the-differences-kitchen.title: Find the Differences Kitchen Pictures for Kids
find-the-differences-kitchen.metaDescription: Find the differences in the kitchen: compare two kitchen scenes and find 3, 7 or 10 differences. Three printable pages for preschool to grade 2.
find-the-differences-kitchen.p1: Pots, cups, plates and a few cheeky mice: these find the differences pages are set in the kitchen. Each page shows the same kitchen scene twice, and some things have changed between the two pictures. Children compare the scenes part by part and mark every difference they find.
find-the-differences-kitchen.p2: There are three pages, each with a different number of differences, which makes them easy to match to the child. Find 3 Differences: Mice in the Kitchen is the gentlest, with big changes and a simple scene. Find 7 Differences: In the Kitchen is an easy page with a classic number of changes. Find 10 Differences: In the Kitchen is at the hard level, with a busier scene and smaller changes. The level is set by how busy the scene is and how big each change is. Each page also has an on-screen version where the child taps the differences.
find-the-differences-kitchen.p3: These pages suit preschool through second grade, with the three-difference page for the youngest children and the ten-difference page as a real challenge. They fit well with a unit on food, cooking or the home. Ask children to name each difference: the cup is missing, the pot is blue now. That turns the puzzle into vocabulary practice as well as a lesson in careful looking.

sight-words-hard.title: Hard Sight Words Worksheets for Grade 1 (PDF)
sight-words-hard.metaDescription: Harder sight words worksheets: longer sentences, capital-letter gaps and look-alike words, plus practice sets. 24 pages for grade 1, printable as PDF.
sight-words-hard.p1: When a child recognizes sight words in short, simple sentences, the next step is reading them anywhere: in longer sentences, at the start of a sentence with a capital letter, and next to words that look almost the same. These harder worksheets give exactly that practice.
sight-words-hard.p2: At the hard level, the sentences are more numerous and longer. Some gaps come at the start of a sentence, so the child has to write the word with a capital letter. Look-alike words appear alongside the sight word, such as was and saw, so children must read carefully rather than guess from the shape. The collection includes Read, Trace, Write pages and sight words practice sets that cover the whole list, so a child meets every word at this level.
sight-words-hard.p3: These pages suit first graders and kindergarteners who are ready for a challenge. When a child mixes up look-alike words, cover all but the first letter and ask what sound it starts with; that usually settles it. The practice sets are a good way to check which words on the list are secure and which still need work. Pair the worksheets with daily reading, where the same words show up in real books.

line-tracing-easy.title: Easy Line Tracing Worksheets for Preschool (PDF)
line-tracing-easy.metaDescription: Easy line tracing worksheets: dashed lines with start dots for zigzags, waves, loops, shapes and picture paths. 24 pages for preschool and K.
line-tracing-easy.p1: Line tracing is where pencil control begins. On these pages, every line in the row is dashed and has its own start dot, and the child follows the dashes across the page: straight lines, zigzags, waves, loops and shapes, often leading from one little picture to the next. These are the movements that later become letters, and practicing them early makes writing easier.
line-tracing-easy.p2: These are all easy-level pages, which means the most help: every repetition in the row is dashed, and each one has its own start dot, so the child always knows where to begin. The collection includes pencil path practice, straight lines and zigzags, wavy lines and curves, down lines, slants and crosses, loops, eights and spirals, circles and squares, picture-to-picture paths and a review page. The pages use many themes, from animals and the beach to bakery treats and the classroom.
line-tracing-easy.p3: Easy line tracing pages suit preschool and kindergarten. Let children trace each line with a finger first, then with a crayon or a thick pencil. Short daily practice works best. When the easy pages go smoothly, the same pages are available at a standard level, with a model and dashed lines, and a hard level, where only the start dots are left and the child draws the line independently.

counting-money-easy.title: Easy Counting Money Worksheets – Coins and Shopping
counting-money-easy.metaDescription: Easy counting money worksheets: fewer and bigger coins, coin purses and shopping math with small prices. 24 printable pages for grades 1-2.
counting-money-easy.p1: Money is math children care about, because it is real: how much is in my purse, and can I buy that? These easy worksheets help children count coins and work out simple prices, with friendly numbers and clear pictures of the coins.
counting-money-easy.p2: There are two kinds of pages. The counting money pages show coin purses to count, including counting coins, coin counting practice, two-coin counting and Which Purse Has More? At the easy level there are fewer coins and they are bigger, so children can count without getting lost. The shopping math pages turn the counting into little shop stories, with prices to add, baskets to total and questions such as "Is there enough money?" At the easy level the prices are smaller. Many pages also have an on-screen version where the child types the answer.
counting-money-easy.p3: These pages suit first and second graders learning coin values and simple money sums. Real or play coins make a great companion: count the purse on the page, then build the same amount with real coins. When the easy level is comfortable, the harder pages use more coins of every kind, bigger prices and change paid with several coins, including the trap where more coins can mean less money.

telling-time-worksheets-hard.title: Hard Telling Time Worksheets – Quarter Past and To
telling-time-worksheets-hard.metaDescription: Harder telling time worksheets: quarter to, five minutes, plain clock faces and common misreadings as options. 24 pages for grades 2-3, as PDF.
telling-time-worksheets-hard.p1: Once children can read o'clock and half past, telling time gets harder in interesting ways: quarter to, five-minute steps, clocks without numbers, and the mistakes everyone makes when the hands are almost on a number. These harder worksheets bring all of that in.
telling-time-worksheets-hard.p2: At the hard level there are more clocks per page. The answer options include the typical misreadings, the hands swapped or the hour before and after, so children have to look carefully at which hand is which. The clock faces are plainer, and the times include quarter to, passing 12 o'clock and durations in quarter hours. The collection includes On the Hour, Half Past What?, Clock Partners, Draw the Clock Hands and Draw the Hands: Five Minutes. Many pages also have an on-screen version where children tap the time, type the hours or drag the hands.
telling-time-worksheets-hard.p3: These pages suit second and third graders. When a child picks a swapped-hands option, ask which hand is longer and what it tells us; that question solves most clock mistakes. A real clock with movable hands on the table is still the best support, even at this level. The duration questions connect telling time to everyday life: how long is it until lunch?

cursive-writing-easy.title: Easy Cursive Writing Worksheets – Letters and Words
cursive-writing-easy.metaDescription: Easy cursive writing worksheets: lowercase and capital letters, first joins and short words, with bigger letters traced twice. 24 pages, as PDF.
cursive-writing-easy.p1: Learning cursive starts with getting each letter right and then learning how letters join. These easy worksheets cover letters from across the alphabet, lowercase letters in the lesson groups schools use and capital letters in alphabet groups, before moving on to joining two letters and writing short words.
cursive-writing-easy.p2: At the easy level the pages give the most support: the letters are bigger, each one is traced twice before the child writes it alone, joins happen at the baseline, words are short, and connecting-letter pages show four pairs. The collection includes lowercase letters such as e, l and b or a, d and g, capital letters in groups, joining two letters, cursive words to write with pictures, and reading cursive, where children match each word to its picture.
cursive-writing-easy.p3: These pages suit second and third graders starting cursive. Practice each letter shape big in the air first, then on the page, and pay attention to where each letter starts. A few letters a day work better than many at once. When the easy pages go smoothly, the harder level has one continuous chain, words printed instead of traced, joins at the top of letters and longer sentences. Praise neat letters often, and let children pick their best letter on each line.

opposites-easy.title: Easy Opposites Worksheets for K-2
opposites-easy.metaDescription: Easy opposites worksheets: picture cues and a word bank, four picture pairs and two words to choose from. 24 pages for kindergarten to grade 2.
opposites-easy.p1: Hot and cold, up and down, full and empty: opposites help children describe the world and compare things. These easy worksheets introduce opposites with lots of support, so every child can succeed and start using the words in their own speech.
opposites-easy.p2: At the easy level each kind of page is made simpler. Write the Opposite Word has picture cues and a word bank. Opposites with Pictures has four picture pairs. Opposites in a Sentence asks children to circle one of two words. Pair Up the Opposites has four pairs. Opposite or the Same? offers two words to choose from. The prefix page, antonyms with un-, dis- and in-, prints the prefix in each row. Many pages also have an on-screen version; Pair Up the Opposites is printable only.
opposites-easy.p3: Most pages suit kindergarten and first grade; the un-, dis- and in- prefix page suits second grade. Act opposites out before the worksheet: stand up tall, crouch down small, open your hands, close them. Movement makes the meaning stick. When the easy pages are comfortable, the hard level removes the word bank and adds more pairs, sentences and words with no partner. Opposite games in the playground, such as fast and slow walking, make a fun follow-up to the worksheet.

color-by-number-rabbit.title: Color by Number Rabbit Worksheets for Kids (PDF)
color-by-number-rabbit.metaDescription: Color by number rabbit pictures: a rabbit in the forest, a rabbit on the farm and a big rabbit picture, at the easy and standard levels. Three pages.
color-by-number-rabbit.p1: Rabbits are a favorite with young children, and these three color by number pages each put a rabbit at the center. Every area of the picture has a number, and the color key shows which color goes with which number. As the child follows the key, the rabbit and its surroundings appear area by area.
color-by-number-rabbit.p2: There are three different pictures: a rabbit in the forest, a rabbit on the farm and a single large rabbit picture. The forest page is at the easy level, with big areas and three to five colors. The other two are at the standard level, with five to seven colors and more parts to color. Each page also has an on-screen version where the child taps an area to fill it with color, which works well on a tablet or an interactive whiteboard.
color-by-number-rabbit.p3: These pages suit preschool, kindergarten and first grade, and they fit naturally into a spring or Easter unit or a theme about animals on the farm and in the forest. Start with the easy forest page, then move on to the other two. Point to each number in the key and name the color together before coloring starts. A finished rabbit makes a cheerful page to take home or to hang in the classroom.
